thesis: Land Tax transforms being behind on lands into repeated card advantage and perfect basic-land access, making deliberate restraint a strategic resource.

canonicalIdentity.originalPrintedText: At the beginning of your upkeep, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may search your library for up to three basic land cards, reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Land Tax shaped early white control, prison, and combo shells, and its interactions with Scroll Rack helped establish a family of engines built around converting redundant cards.

playbook.role: Stay behind on land count when the trigger is worth more than the next land drop, and combine the fetched basics with Scroll Rack, discard outlets, or effects that turn excess cards into value.
